'''Microsoft Power BI''' ('''PBI''') is an interactive [[data visualization]], database management, and data modeling software product developed by [[Microsoft]] with a primary focus on [[business intelligence]] (BI).<ref>{{cite web |title=Bring your data to life with Microsoft Power BI |url=https://powerbi.microsoft.com/en-us/ |website=Microsoft.com |publisher=Microsoft |access-date=4 May 2016 |archive-date=27 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190527023619/https://powerbi.microsoft.com/en-us/ |url-status=live }}</ref> It is part of the [[Microsoft Power Platform]].

Power BI is a collection of [[software]] services, apps, and connectors that work together to turn various sources of data into static and interactive data visualizations. Data may be input by reading directly from a [[database]], webpage, [[PDF]], or structured files such as spreadsheets, [[Comma-separated values|CSV]], [[XML]],  [[JSON]],<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=31 March 2023 |title=List of all Power Query connectors - Power Query |url=https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/connectors/ |access-date=11 July 2023 |website=learn.microsoft.com |language=en-us |archive-date=11 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230711044833/https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/connectors/ |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Microsoft Excel|XLSX]], and [[SharePoint]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 August 2023 |title=How to Design Power BI Dashboard: A Step-by-Step Guide |url=https://lookuplinks.com/how-to-design-power-bi-dashboard |access-date=24 September 2023 |website=lookuplinks.com |archive-date=26 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230926172712/https://lookuplinks.com/how-to-design-power-bi-dashboard/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==General==
Power BI provides [[cloud computing|cloud]]-based BI (business intelligence) services, known as "Power BI Services", along with a desktop-based interface, called "Power BI Desktop". It provides [[data warehouse]] capabilities including [[data preparation]], [[data mining]], and interactive dashboards.<ref name="Gartner BI Magic Quadrant">{{cite web |title=Magic Quadrant for Business Intelligence and Analytics Platforms |url=https://www.gartner.com/doc/reprints?id=1-2XYY9ZR&ct=160204&st=sb |website=Gartner.com |publisher=Gartner, Inc. |access-date=4 May 2016 |archive-date=29 May 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180529113602/https://www.gartner.com/doc/reprints?id=1-2XYY9ZR&ct=160204&st=sb |url-status=live }}</ref>

In March 2016, Microsoft released an additional service called Power BI Embedded on its [[Microsoft Azure|Azure]] cloud platform.<ref>{{cite web |last=Caldwell |first=Nick |date=31 March 2016 |title=Embed the wow of Power BI in your applications with Microsoft Power BI Embedded! |url=https://powerbi.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/embed-the-wow-of-power-bi-in-your-applications-with-microsoft-power-bi-embedded/ |website=Powerbi.microsoft.com |publisher=Microsoft |access-date=4 May 2016 |archive-date=18 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190218202039/https://powerbi.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/embed-the-wow-of-power-bi-in-your-applications-with-microsoft-power-bi-embedded/ |url-status=live }}</ref> One main differentiator of the product is the ability to load custom visualizations.

==History==
The software was originally used as Power Pivot and Power Query in Microsoft Excel. This application was originally conceived by Thierry D'Hers and Amir Netz of the [[SQL Server Reporting Services]] team at Microsoft.<ref>{{cite web |title=A Glimpse at Project Crescent |url=https://blogs.msdn.microsoft.com/sqlrsteamblog/2010/11/09/a-glimpse-at-project-crescent/ |website=Microsoft BI Blog |date=9 November 2010 |publisher=Microsoft |access-date=29 June 2017 |archive-date=24 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160324093147/https://blogs.msdn.microsoft.com/sqlrsteamblog/2010/11/09/a-glimpse-at-project-crescent/ |url-status=live }}</ref>  It was originally designed by Ron George in the summer of 2010 and named Project Crescent.<ref>{{cite web |title=Data Visualization Done Right: Project Crescent |url=https://blogs.msdn.microsoft.com/bi/2010/11/09/data-visualization-done-right-project-crescent/ |website=Microsoft BI Blog |date=9 November 2010 |publisher=Microsoft |access-date=29 June 2017 |archive-date=31 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170831221803/https://blogs.msdn.microsoft.com/bi/2010/11/09/data-visualization-done-right-project-crescent/ |url-status=live }}</ref>  Project Crescent was initially available for public download on 11 July 2011, bundled with SQL Server Codename Denali.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Unkroth |first1=Kay |title=Announcing Microsoft SQL Server Code Name "Denali" Community Technology Preview 3 (CTP3) |url=https://blogs.msdn.microsoft.com/analysisservices/2011/07/12/announcing-microsoft-sql-server-code-name-denali-community-technology-preview-3-ctp3/ |website=blogs.msdn.microsoft.com |date=12 July 2011 |publisher=Microsoft |access-date=28 May 2019 |archive-date=25 April 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170425115552/https://blogs.msdn.microsoft.com/analysisservices/2011/07/12/announcing-microsoft-sql-server-code-name-denali-community-technology-preview-3-ctp3/ |url-status=live }}</ref>  Later renamed Power BI it was then unveiled by Microsoft in September 2013 as Power BI for [[Microsoft 365|Office 365]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Office 365 Gets Colorful 3D Charts, Natural Language Search |url=http://in.pcmag.com/productivity/70071/news/office-365-gets-colorful-3d-charts-natural-languag |website=PC Mag India |date=26 September 2013 |publisher=ZiffDavis, LLC PCMag India |access-date=4 May 2016 |archive-date=16 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191216215845/https://in.pcmag.com/productivity/70071/office-365-gets-colorful-3d-charts-natural-language-search |url-status=dead }}</ref>  The first release of Power BI was based on the [[Microsoft Excel]]-based add-ins: [[Power Query]], [[Power Pivot]] and Power View. With time, Microsoft also added many additional features like question and answers, enterprise-level data connectivity, and security options via Power BI Gateways.<ref name="Gartner BI Magic Quadrant" /> Power BI was first released to the general public on 24 July 2015. It has several versions for desktop, web, and mobile app.<ref>{{cite web |last=The Power BI Team |first=Microsoft |date=10 July 2015 |title=Announcing Power BI general availability coming July 24th |url=https://powerbi.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/announcing-power-bi-general-availability-coming-july-24th/ |website=Microsoft Power BI Blog |publisher=Microsoft |access-date=4 May 2016 |archive-date=12 August 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210812081334/https://powerbi.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/announcing-power-bi-general-availability-coming-july-24th/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 14 April 2015, Microsoft announced that they had acquired the Canadian company Datazen, to "complement Power BI, our cloud-based business analytics service, rounding out our mobile capabilities for customers who need a mobile BI solution implemented on-premises and optimized for [[Microsoft SQL Server|SQL Server]]."
<ref name="Microsoft acquires mobile business intelligence leader Datazen">{{cite web |last=Hathi |first=Kamal |date=14 April 2015 |title=Microsoft acquires mobile business intelligence leader Datazen |url=https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2015/04/14/microsoft-acquires-mobile-business-intelligence-leader-datazen/ |website=blogs.microsoft.com |publisher=Microsoft, Inc. |access-date=10 January 2022 |archive-date=10 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220110122409/https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2015/04/14/microsoft-acquires-mobile-business-intelligence-leader-datazen/ |url-status=live }}</ref>  Most of the 'visuals' in Power BI started life as Datazen visuals.

==Key components==
[[File:Qué Productos se Venden Juntos de la Solución Past2Future Business Intelligence.jpg|thumb|right|Example of a screenshot from the software]]

Key components of the Power BI ecosystem are as follows:
; Power BI Desktop<ref>{{Cite book |last=Hyman |first=Jack |title=Microsoft Power BI for dummies |date=8 February 2022 |publisher=wiley |isbn=978-1-119-82487-9 |location=NJ |pages=47–62}}</ref>: The Windows desktop-based application for PCs, primarily for designing and publishing reports to the service.
; Power BI Service : The [[Software as a service|SaaS-based (software as a service)]] online service. This was formerly known as Power BI for Office 365, now referred to as PowerBI.com or simply Power BI.
; Power BI Mobile Apps: Power BI Mobile apps are for Android and iOS devices, as well as for Windows phones and tablets.
; Power BI Gateway: Gateways are used to sync external data in and out of Power BI and are required for automated refreshes. In enterprise mode, it can also be used by [[Microsoft Power Automate]] (previously called Flows) and PowerApps in Office 365.
; Power BI Embedded: Power BI [[REST]] API can be used to build dashboards and reports into the custom applications that serve Power BI users and non-Power BI users.
; Power BI Report Server: An [[On-premises software|on-premises]] Power BI is a reporting product for companies that choose not to store data in the cloud-based Power BI Service.
; Power BI Premium: Capacity-based offering that includes flexibility to publish reports broadly across an enterprise without requiring recipients to be licensed individually per user. This provides greater scale and performance than shared capacity in the Power BI Service.
; Power BI Visuals Marketplace: A marketplace of custom visuals and [[R (programming language)|R-powered]] visuals.<ref>{{cite web |date=25 December 2017 |title=Power BI Custom visuals on AppSource |url=https://appsource.microsoft.com/en-us/marketplace/apps?product=power-bi-visuals |website=Microsoft AppSource |publisher=Microsoft |access-date=25 December 2017 |archive-date=26 December 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171226020952/https://appsource.microsoft.com/en-us/marketplace/apps?product=power-bi-visuals |url-status=live }}</ref>
; Power BI Dataflow<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/transform-model/dataflows/dataflows-create |title=Creating a dataflow - Power BI {{!}} Microsoft Docs |access-date=24 February 2022 |archive-date=24 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220224092651/https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/transform-model/dataflows/dataflows-create |url-status=live }}</ref>: A Power Query implementation in the cloud that can be used for data transformations to make a common Power BI Semantic Model, which can then be made available for report developers through Microsoft's Common Data Service. For example, it can be used as an alternative to doing transformations in [[Microsoft Analysis Services|SSAS]] and may ensure that several report developers use data that has been transformed similarly.
; Power BI Semantic Model<ref>{{Cite web |title=Datasets renamed to semantic models |url=https://powerbi.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/datasets-renamed-to-semantic-models/ |access-date=2025-07-03 |website=powerbi.microsoft.com |language=en}}</ref>: A Power BI Semantic Model (formerly Dataset) can work as a collection of data for use in Power BI reports, and can either be connected to or imported into a Power BI Report.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Get started |first=Power BI |date=3 October 2022 |title=Basic concepts for designers in the Power BI service |url=https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/fundamentals/service-basic-concepts |access-date=4 April 2022 |archive-date=24 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220324063054/https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/fundamentals/service-basic-concepts |url-status=live }}</ref> A semantic model can be connected to and get its source data through one or more dataflows.
; Power BI Datamart: Within Power BI, the datamart is a container that combines Power BI Dataflows, datasets, and a type of [[data mart]] or [[data warehouse]] (in the form of an [[Microsoft Azure SQL Database|Azure SQL Database]]) into the same interface. The interface then has the possibility of being a single place for the administration of both the ETL layer ([[Dataflow]]), an intermediary data mart (with for instance storage of [[star schema]]s, [[dimension table]]s, [[fact table]]s), and finally the [[Data modeling|modeling layer]] (dataset).
; Power BI Datahub: A [[data hub]] for discovering Power BI datasets within an organization's Power BI Service so that datasets may be reused from one central location. It offers details on the things as well as an access point for working with them, such as building reports on top of them, utilizing them with Excel's Analyze feature, accessing settings, controlling permissions, and more.<ref>{{Cite web |last=paulinbar |title=Data discovery using the data hub - Power BI |url=https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/service-data-hub |access-date=11 March 2023 |website=learn.microsoft.com |language=en-us |archive-date=11 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230311235540/https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/service-data-hub |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Power Query ===
{{Further|Power Query}}
[[Extract, transform, load|ETL]] processes in both the web and desktop versions of Power BI are facilitated in Power Query through built-in connectors to pull data from a wide variety of sources. Power Query provides a [[GUI]] which allows users to perform many common data preparation operations without needing to write code, though more advanced operations may be performed through expressions written in the M formula language.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Puls |first=Ken |title=Master Your Data with Excel and Power BI: Leveraging Power Query to Get & Transform Your Task Flow; Formerly M is for Data Monkey |last2=Escobar |first2=Miguel |date=2021 |publisher=Holy Macro! Books |isbn=978-1-61547-058-7 |edition=2nd |location=Chicago}}</ref>

== Licenses ==
Power BI has several different licenses depending on your specific use case.  You should note however, as of June 2026, you need a work or school email to sign up for a license that will enable development or publishing.  This includes, creating dashboards, publishing or sharing dashboards, and creating the underlying semantic models.<ref>{{Cite web |last=JulCsc |title=Licenses and Subscriptions for Business Users - Power BI |url=https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/fundamentals/end-user-license |access-date=2026-06-17 |website=learn.microsoft.com |language=en-us}}</ref>

=== User licenses ===
Currently, Microsoft Power BI offers ''free, Pro, and Premium Per User'' licenses. Users who own or administer their Microsoft Tenant are allowed a single developer license for free. Free users must be part of an organization with a Power BI license. They can consume reports, and can also build, but not publish. In practice, creators need at least a pro license ($14.00/month) in order to publish reports, and premium users ($24.00/month) can publish in the same manner as a pro license, but also have more features available for developing.<ref>{{Cite web |last=JulCsc |title=Sign Up or Purchase Power BI as an Individual - Power BI |url=https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/fundamentals/service-self-service-signup-purchase-for-power-bi |access-date=2026-06-17 |website=learn.microsoft.com |language=en-us}}</ref>

=== Workspace licenses ===
''Premium capacity'' refers to the license of the workspace, not the licenses of its users or creators. Also, access to several features, functionalities, and kinds of content that are exclusively accessible through premium is made possible with a Power BI Premium per-user license.<ref>{{Cite web |last=kfollis |title=Power BI service features by license type - Power BI |url=https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/fundamentals/service-features-license-type |access-date=27 November 2022 |website=learn.microsoft.com |language=en-us |archive-date=27 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221127025315/https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/fundamentals/service-features-license-type |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Premium per user'' is a special workspace license which was added in November 2020,<ref name="element61">[https://www.element61.be/en/resource/theres-power-bi-flavor-every-organization-meet-power-bi-premium-user Meet Power BI Premium per user element61]</ref> and can be a more affordable alternative to premium workspace licenses for organizations with few users which have advanced analytical requirements.<ref name="element61"/>

== Paginated reports ==
{{further|SQL Server Reporting Services#Power BI Report Builder}}
[[Financial reporting|Paginated report]]s for Power BI, which can be built with Power BI Report Builder, are a special type of SSRS reports with [[pagination]] formatting which can give better control of the layout of reports which need to be printed to paper or PDF. This is in contrast to regular Power BI reports which instead are optimized for presentation or interactivity and exploration on a screen. Paginated reports can, as of 2022, not be made with the regular ''Power BI Desktop'' report builder software. Instead, the standalone ''Power BI Report Builder'' has to be used, which can be viewed as a descendant of the [[SQL Server Reporting Services]] (SSRS) ''Microsoft Report Builder'' for [[Microsoft SQL Server]] introduced in 2004. It is also similar to the ''Report Designer'' in SQL Server Data Tools.

Power BI Paginated reports are saved in the [[Report Definition Language]] (.rdl file format), as opposed to the .pbix file of regular Power BI reports or the recently introduced .pbir format.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Power BI's Enhanced Report Format (PBIR) - Acuity Training |url=https://www.acuitytraining.co.uk/news-tips/power-bis-enhanced-report-format-pbir/ |access-date=2025-09-09 |website=www.acuitytraining.co.uk}}</ref> The RDL format is based on XML and was proposed by Microsoft as a benchmark for defining reports with SSRS.

Paginated reports may be more suitable than regular Power BI reports, and may include printing of invoices or other repeated printouts of reports with a similar layout but different content, or for printing reports where text would otherwise overflow due to being cut off by scrollbars.
